The equipment reads THROUGH the glass: the red/blue PDU pair, the upper device, the stacked base units. Criticals stay 100% eye-visible through the glass, so eye-sight and click-reach coincide.

important_features.note: Glass door on the hero cabinet makes the glass-LED read AND the transparency pick rule bearing.

defects: Aisle length still confidence:low; bar/stools masses (declared).

mechanical.notes: 0 guard failures; boot clean; interaction pass from BOTH views; negative control 13/13 PLUS the reconstructed PDU defect caught 4x. THE TWO CARRIED RULES, finally exercised for real: (1) the pick stops at the first OPAQUE surface (Stratix port), and the PDU defect IS REAL here — a neighbouring cabinet's opaque non-hotspot side panel is exactly the occluder the isolated PDU could never manifest (there every occluder was itself a hotspot). (2) a click passes through TRANSPARENT surfaces and stops at the first opaque, glass pickable at LOW priority. TO MAKE THE TRANSPARENCY RULE BEARING NOT THEORETICAL: the hero cabinet now shows its glass door (the rack's own Variant B) — with all doors opaque there was NO glass in front of any device and the carried rule would have shipped UNEXERCISED (a rule nothing exercises is not known to work). FINDINGS: the negative control first read the guard as DEAD and was wrong — from the HERO-RACK view the defective pick fired 0 (the only thing between camera and UPS is the glass, which both correct and defective picks pass through), so the SPECIMEN could not contain the defect; from the AISLE view it fires 4x ('ups clickable although side_panels is opaque and in front'). A control tests an instrument on the case it was built from, and the case must actually be present. REACHED-BY-RAY IS NOT CLICKABLE: the probe reported the ceiling camera clickable at (3383,-5553) on a 1600x900 viewport — nothing opaque in front so the ray arrived, but no cursor can go off-frame; now discarded as offscreen. A CONSTANT NOTHING VALIDATED: PASSES checked the query param but never CURRENT_PASS, so 'LIGHTING-CAMERA' sat a whole pass as a non-member (the HUD label still rendered, so internal inconsistency, not a visible defect) — the inversion is that the OUTSIDE value was protected and the LOCAL (highest-change-rate, human-edited) value trusted; now asserted. And the process note that let it hide: it only surfaced because the boot ran AFTER the edit this time — a verification that precedes the edit it should cover verifies nothing (owned in the WORK ORDER, not just the code). GUARDS: verifyPickCannotReachThroughSolids states the RESULT property (true however the pick is rewritten); verifyClickAgreesWithSight is RELATIONAL (pick vs the visibility check, can't drift to disagreeing about the same glass, and fails if the scene has NO visible transparent surface, because then the rule is untested). Both run AT BOOT, not only under probe — a rule checked only when someone remembers is how the PDU shipped a through-solids pick.

notes: Inline orchestrator judgment. The two rules carried across the whole run from the PDU and Axis finally land where they are load-bearing: the PDU's opaque-occluder defect is real in an aisle (a neighbour's side panel), and the Axis transparency rule needed a glass door in front of a device to be exercised at all — supplied through the rack's OWN Variant B, not a scene edit. The pass is thick with epistemic care: a negative control that read dead because its specimen could not hold the defect, a probe that returned an off-frame 'clickable' point no cursor can reach, and a CURRENT_PASS constant that nothing validated because verification ran before the edit — each owned precisely and fixed at the right level. The new guards are result-property and relational (the forms established this run that cannot go stale) and run at boot. Cleared to the optimization pass.
